samples.summary: The new `requestLayoutRefresh` seam (layout must still refresh while a render is held inside an open undo unit) has no test anywhere
samples.evidence: This delta adds `requestLayoutRefresh?: () => void` (text-editor.ts:233), calls it from the held-render branch (text-editor.ts:738), and wires it in the docs host (editor.ts:2531). The lessons doc (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-select-all-type-undo-lessons.md:37-45) describes the concrete user-visible defect it fixes: with the render held, the rest of the unit kept reading a pre-delete `blockParentMap`, which the paste path branches on (`isInCell`/`getCellInfo`), so a paste over a selection inside/near a table cell takes the wrong branch. No test exercises this: grepping `requestLayoutRefresh|recomputeLayout|blockParentMap` under packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests turns up only unrelated layout fixtures; the new frontend test only counts paints (ctx.save), never asserts the layout/`blockParentMap` was refreshed mid-unit, and no test constructs a paste-into-cell after a batched delete. The regression would silently reappear (and be data-affecting for pasted content) with the whole suite green — and it is invisible to every mechanical lane.

samples.summary: The "held, not swallowed … shows the committed state" assertion in the paint-count test does not test ordering; it re-asserts store state already covered elsewhere
samples.evidence: `expect(texts()).toEqual(['X'])` reads the store after the action; it holds whether the single paint ran before or after the batch committed, and whether the paint saw the committed layout at all. The identical assertion already exists at line 341 in 'replaces the whole document for one undo unit'. The paint-ordering claim in the comment ('shows the committed state rather than the pre-edit one') is therefore unverified — a real assertion would have to capture the layout/text observed during the paint (e.g. via the shim's fillText calls) rather than the post-hoc store.

samples.summary: No test covers the documented 'held render is replayed once, including after a throw' branch of withUndoUnit
samples.evidence: withUndoUnit's doc comment claims interior renders are replayed 'at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw, so the screen always shows what the store really holds'. The new paint-count test (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:363) only covers the success path. Nothing in packages/docs/test or packages/frontend/tests drives a throwing body through withUndoUnit and asserts a paint still happened; a lost replay leaves the canvas showing a stale document after a failed edit.

samples.summary: MemDocStore checkpoint adoption is tested for undo only — no test covers redo after an adopted batch
samples.evidence: The three new cases (memory.test.ts:317, 339, 353) assert undo depth/content after `snapshot(); batch(...)`, but none does `snapshot(); batch(write); undo(); redo()`. The adoption path shares the stack-top object by reference (`const before = adopted ? top : beforeClone`, memory.ts:224) and `wroteNothing` may `pop()` a checkpoint it did not push (memory.ts:252), so redo-stack behaviour around adoption is exactly the part most likely to be wrong and is unasserted. Existing redo coverage in this describe block ('a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact', line ~373) does not use the snapshot-before-batch ordering.

samples.summary: Using `ctxCalls.save === 1` as a paint counter is only valid because jsdom's zero-sized canvas culls every page
samples.evidence: `DocCanvas.paint` calls `ctx.save()` once at line 256 but again per rendered page (doc-canvas.ts:269, 290, 338, ...), and the shim returns the same proxy context for every canvas, so the ruler/table renderers count too. The '=1 per paint' invariant the comment asserts holds only while the page loop is fully culled (viewportHeight 0 in jsdom); any layout/paint change makes this count internal saves instead of paints, and the test then reports a paint-deferral regression that isn't one (or hides one that is).

finding.summary: New render-deferral wrapper around `requestRender` has no test at all
finding.evidence: The diff introduces a `requestRender` wrapper (text-editor.ts:718-724) that swallows every interior render while `undoUnitDepth > 0` and replays it once in `withUndoUnit`'s `finally` (3819-3822). Grepping the whole repo for `withUndoUnit|renderAfterUndoUnit|undoUnitDepth|hostRequestRender` returns hits only in src/view/text-editor.ts — no test file references them. The only new tests (editor-undo-selection.test.ts #1045 block, yorkie-doc-store.test.ts) assert store contents and undo-stack depth; none observe paint. If the replay ever fails to fire (e.g. depth never returning to 0, or the flag being cleared on the wrong path), every keystroke, Enter, paste and IME commit would leave the canvas stale — highly user-visible — and nothing in the suite would go red.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the withUndoUnit render-deferral wrapper has no test observing paint. A test exists that does exactly that: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts:363-372 ("paints once for the whole action, after the unit commits") resets a canvas-shim call counter and asserts ctxCalls.save === 1 after typing over a select-all. The shim (lines 45-91, counter increment at line 73) records every 2D-context method call, and save fires once per paint() pass, so the assertion fails at 2 if the hold does not engage and fails at 0 if the replay in withUndoUnit's finally never fires — the exact stale-canvas regression the finding says nothing would catch. The test-file comment at 358-362 documents this intent, and the reviewer's own grep term `withUndoUnit` hits that comment line in this test file; their search set simply omitted the observable (ctxCalls/ctx.save). The claim that "none observe paint" is contradicted inside the file cited as evidence.

finding.summary: Doc claims paste is now "One undo unit … Pinned by editor-undo-selection.test.ts", but that test only asserts the cost is ≤ 6 and constant
finding.evidence: applyPastePlan's docstring was rewritten from "Not one undo unit" to "One undo unit … Pinned by `tests/app/docs/editor-undo-selection.test.ts`". That test (editor-undo-selection.test.ts:200-220) asserts only `expect(large).toBe(small)` and `expect(small).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6)` — it passes identically whether a paste costs 1 unit or 4, so the newly-claimed one-unit property is not pinned and a regression back to multiple `doc.update()`s per paste is invisible. The test was not updated in this diff. Additionally every paste in that test uses a *collapsed* selection, so the newly-batched "delete selection + paste" combination (the case that can overflow the 50-entry cap and lose the replaced content, exactly the #1045 failure mode) is never exercised.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence does not match this repository. (1) The claimed weak assertion `expect(small).toBeLessThanOrEqual(6)` does not exist — a repo-wide grep for `toBeLessThanOrEqual` under packages/frontend/tests/app/docs returns only an unrelated hit in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2293. What the test actually asserts at editor-undo-selection.test.ts:237 is `expect(small).toBe(1)`, an exact equality on the absolute undo cost, with an inline comment stating a ceiling was deliberately avoided because it "would let a regression to 4 pass." So the newly-claimed one-unit property IS pinned, and a regression to multiple doc.update()s per paste fails loudly. (2) The claim that "every paste in that test uses a collapsed selection" is false: the second test in the same describe block, 'a paste over a multi-block selection is one undo unit' (lines 240-267), constructs a range spanning from blocks[0] offset 0 to the end of the last block (lines 248-254), passes it through the `range` parameter of `pasteHtml` (lines 197-205), asserts the composite delete+insert costs exactly `before + 1` (line 261), and asserts a single `editor.undo()` restores the full text of every original block (lines 263-266). That is exactly the #1045 delete-selection-plus-paste failure mode the finding says is never exercised. The docstring at text-editor.ts:1532-1542 claims precisely what these two tests assert.
